2. The relevant facts, in short, are that, the petitioner as preemptor instituted the aforesaid Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 29 of 2003 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act praying for Pre-emption of the case land. The preempted opposite party appeared in the case. Accordingly, the case proceeded in accordance with law and in course of trial both the parties examined witnesses to prove their respective claim. 

 3. Thereafter, at the stage of peremptory hearing of the case the pre-emptor-petitioner filed an application under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the learned District Judge, Narayangonj for transferring the preemption case from the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court. Narayangonj to any other appropriate Court. However, the learned District Judge, Narayangonj after hearing the parties was pleased to reject the said application on the sole finding that the allegation as stated in the application is based on mere surmise and conjecture without any material basis whatsoever. 

 6. In this Rule the petitioner has come up with an allegation of bias against the presiding judge of the trial Court. Before this Court in the application it has been stated that after taking certified copy of the depositions of the plaintiff's witnesses, the petitioner came to know that many material statements made by the witnesses in the depositions were not recorded which led to an apprehension that if the case is tried by the Court he will not be fairly and impartially treated: 

 7. On the other hand, from Annexure’ A' 7 i.e. the application filed under section 24 of the Code before the learned District Judge, it appears that the petitioner filed the aforesaid application on the ground that the defendant-opposite party in the Court premises openly stated that by any means he will win the case. It is also stated that the presiding Judge is a close relative of Mr. Alauddin Sarder, the Law Secretary of the Government. 

 8. But neither before the learned District Judge nor before this Court it has been specifically mentioned what statement/statements of the witnesses have been omitted by the presiding Judge at the time of recording the evidence. Moreover, although it has been asserted that the presiding judge is a close relative of the present Law Secretary, but what is the relationship between them has not been disclosed. Besides, no name of any disinterested person has been mentioned in the application who have heard the aforesaid statement, that by any means he will win the case. 

 10. Now the only question that calls for determination by this Court is, as to whether the plaintiff-petitioner has been able to make out a case for transfer. It is now well settled that in an application for transfer heavy onus lies on the petitioner to show that there is bias in the presiding judge. We have already indicated that all the allegations including the omission to record the evidence are absolutely vague and indefinite and no material whatsoever was either placed before the learned District Judge along with the application filed before him to substantiate the allegations. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears to us that the learned District Judge rightly observed that there is no basis in the allegation of bias and it is the product of mere surmises and conjecture without any material basis. On consideration of the materials on record and after considering the statement made by the learned Advocates for the parties, we do not find any cogent reason to take a different view and it appears to us that the petitioner has miserably failed to show any omission or bias against the presiding judge.
